title: Isomorphism spaces of objects of an algebraic stack are locally of finite type
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$, $T$ an $S$-scheme, and $a,b\in\mathcal X(T)$. The sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X,T}(a,b)$ on $T$-schemes, sending $T'\to T$ to the isomorphisms $a_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}b_{T'}$ in $\mathcal X(T')$, is an algebraic space locally of finite type over $T$. In particular this holds for the automorphism group algebraic space $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal X,T}(a)=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X,T}(a,a)$, with multiplication given by composition. An algebraic stack here is a stack in groupoids on schemes over $S$ with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Fibred groupoids, stacks, representability and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Smoothness and surjectivity of a representable map are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts, using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and ordinary surjectivity on points. Locally of finite type for algebraic spaces is tested etale locally on source and target using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 04XR (lemma-isom-locally-finite-type), and the representability convention immediately preceding it.

proof.text: Put $I=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X,T}(a,b)$. It is the base change of the representable diagonal along $(a,b):T\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$, hence an algebraic space. Explicitly, over a test scheme $H\to T$, an object of that 2-base change is $(c,\alpha:c\xrightarrow{\sim}a_H,\beta:c\xrightarrow{\sim}b_H)$. Send it to $\beta\alpha^{-1}$. Conversely an isomorphism $\gamma:a_H\to b_H$ gives $(a_H,1,\gamma)$. Any object mapping to $\gamma$ is uniquely isomorphic to this one, by $\alpha$. These mutually inverse identifications commute with pullback, so identify the discrete fibred groupoid of $I$ with that 2-base change. This uses exactly the representable-diagonal hypothesis and the stated definition of 2-fibre products; no finite-type assertion has yet been used.

source.place: Tag 04XR, paragraph preceding lemma-isom-locally-finite-type; stacks.tex Tag 04SI (lemma-isom-as-2-fibre-product).

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal X$. Let $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$, with an $H$-point written $(u,v,\gamma:p(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}p(v))$. The diagonal hypothesis makes $R$ an algebraic space, by base change along $U\times_SU\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$. Each projection $s,t:R\to U$ is a base change of $p$, and is smooth: the hypothesis that $p$ is smooth is, by the statement's convention, precisely the assertion that its scheme base changes are smooth on etale scheme charts. In particular, for any etale scheme chart $V\to R$, the composite $V\to R\xrightarrow{s}U$ is smooth. This is the atlas relation used in the proof of Tag 04T5; no quotient-stack equivalence is needed here.

source.place: Tags 04T4 (lemma-map-space-into-stack), (1) and its triples description, and 04T5 (lemma-stack-presentation), proof of smoothness of s,t.

proof.text: The relation map $r=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ is locally of finite type. Indeed, take any etale scheme chart $V\to R$. The smooth composite $V\to U$ is locally of finite presentation by the definition of smoothness. In the affine presentations defining this property, the coordinate algebra is $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$, hence is generated by the images of $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ as an $A$-algebra. Thus $V\to U$ is locally of finite type. Apply clause (a) of [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target] to the scheme morphisms $V\to U\times_SU\to U$. It gives that $V\to U\times_SU$ is locally of finite type. Since this holds on every such chart, it gives the assertion about $r$ by the chartwise definition. No separation of $U\to S$ is required.

source.place: Tag 04XR (lemma-isom-locally-finite-type), final sentences; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 04AJ, 0464 and 0462. Here cancellation is applied to schemes on etale charts.

proof.text: Form $E_a=T\times_{a,\mathcal X,p}U$. Explicitly this is the base change of the diagonal of $\mathcal X$ along $(a\circ\operatorname{pr}_T,p\circ\operatorname{pr}_U):T\times_SU\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$: its test objects are $(h,u,\alpha:p(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}a(h))$. Thus $E_a$ is an algebraic space by the diagonal hypothesis, while $E_a\to T$ is smooth and surjective by the atlas hypothesis. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $T_1\to E_a$. By the convention for smooth maps to a scheme, $q_1:T_1\to T$ is smooth, and it is surjective since both maps are surjective on point classes. The chart specifies a lift $u_1:T_1\to U$ and an isomorphism $p(u_1)\cong a_{T_1}$. Next form $E_b=T_1\times_{b_{T_1},\mathcal X,p}U$ and choose a surjective etale scheme chart $T_2\to E_b$. The same reasoning gives a smooth surjective scheme morphism $q_2:T_2\to T_1$ and a lift $v_2:T_2\to U$ of $b_{T_2}$. Pulling back $u_1$ gives a lift $u_2$ of $a_{T_2}$. Each $q_i$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. We keep these two successive covers separate and will descend twice.

source.place: Tag 04T5 (lemma-stack-presentation), proof, local lifting through a smooth surjective atlas; used in stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 04XR.

proof.text: Both singleton families $\{q_i\}$ are fpqc coverings, even though $q_i$ need not be quasi-compact. To check this directly, write $q:V\to B$ for either $q_i$. It is flat and locally of finite presentation, so it is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. For an affine open $A\subset B$, choose an affine open cover $q^{-1}(A)=\bigcup_jV_j$. Surjectivity and openness give the open covering $A=\bigcup_j q(V_j)$. The affine scheme $A$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so finitely many of these images cover $A$. Flatness together with this finite-affine-image condition is exactly [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. This is the proof of Topologies Tag 022C, with the needed openness and compactness explicitly cited.

Fix the lift isomorphisms $\alpha:p(u_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}a_{T_2}$ and $\beta:p(v_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}b_{T_2}$. There is an isomorphism of algebraic spaces over $T_2$
$$I\times_TT_2\cong T_2\times_{(u_2,v_2),U\times_SU,r}R.$$
For each $H\to T_2$, send $\delta:a_H\xrightarrow{\sim}b_H$ to the point of $R$ with coordinates $(u_{2,H},v_{2,H},\beta_H^{-1}\delta\alpha_H)$. Conversely send $(u_{2,H},v_{2,H},\gamma)$ to $\beta_H\gamma\alpha_H^{-1}$. These formulas are inverse and commute with restriction in $H$. Hence they define inverse natural transformations, which are morphisms of algebraic spaces by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Fibre products of the spaces here exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. This proves the local identification rather than invoking a quotient-stack presentation theorem.

source.place: Tag 04XR (lemma-isom-locally-finite-type), Isom fibre-product formula; algebraic.tex Tag 04T4, description of R by triples. The source uses (target,source); here R is parametrized by (source,target), so the order is (u_2,v_2).

proof.text: The morphism on the right of the displayed identification is a base change of $r$, proved locally of finite type in step 3. An algebraic space, viewed as a discrete fibred groupoid, is a Deligne--Mumford stack: its sheaf descent gives stack descent, its diagonal is representable, and its defining surjective etale scheme chart is a DM atlas. Apply the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], in its stated algebraic-space case: it identifies the stack and ordinary algebraic-space notions and preserves local finite type under arbitrary base change. Consequently $I\times_TT_2\to T_2$ is locally of finite type. Both its target $T_2$ and the target $U\times_SU$ of $r$ are schemes, and every space in this base change is an algebraic space; no general algebraic-stack base-change theorem is being applied to an unverified stack.

source.place: Tag 03XH (lemma-base-change-finite-type); used in stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 04XR after the Isom fibre-product formula.

proof.text: Take any etale scheme chart $Z\to I$. Put $Z_1=Z\times_TT_1$ and $Z_2=Z_1\times_{T_1}T_2$, which are scheme fibre products. The fibre-product universal property identifies $Z_2$ with $(I\times_TT_2)\times_I Z$: on a test scheme both specify a point of $Z$ and a point of $T_2$ with the same image in $T$. The maps are the pair of projections and their unique inverse supplied by the fibre-product universal property; their composites are identities because both preserve these projections. Thus $Z_2\to I\times_TT_2$ is precisely the base change of $Z\to I$, and is an etale scheme chart by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. The preceding step and the chartwise meaning of local finite type imply that the scheme morphism $Z_2\to T_2$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-locally-finite-type] first to $Z_1\to T_1$ and the fpqc covering $\{q_2:T_2\to T_1\}$ from step 5. This gives that $Z_1\to T_1$ is locally of finite type. Apply the same node to $Z\to T$ and $\{q_1:T_1\to T\}$ to get that $Z\to T$ is locally of finite type. Since $Z\to I$ was arbitrary, $I\to T$ is locally of finite type by the stated algebraic-space convention. The descent node is used only on scheme morphisms, as its statement requires.

source.place: Tag 041S (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-type), chartwise reduction to descent.tex Tag 02KX (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-type); same reduction as the proof of 041S.

proof.text: Set $b=a$. The preceding conclusion gives the algebraic space $G=\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal X,T}(a)$ locally of finite type over $T$. On each $H\to T$, define $G(H)\times G(H)\to G(H)$ by composition, $G(H)\to G(H)$ by inversion, and the identity by $1_{a_H}$. Pullback in the fibred groupoid preserves these operations, so these are natural transformations, hence morphisms of algebraic spaces. Their group identities hold on every test scheme because they are the associativity, identity and inverse identities in the groupoid $\mathcal X(H)$. Thus this is the claimed automorphism group algebraic space, with the specified multiplication.

lean.statement: theorem moduli_isom_space_locallyOfFiniteType {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) (T : Over S) (a b : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) F) : (∃ I : ModuliIsomSpace T a b, ∀ (V : Over S) (c : yoneda.obj V ⟶ I.space.obj.obj), AlgebraicSpace.IsEtale c → LocallyOfFiniteType ((yoneda.preimage (c ≫ I.projection)).left)) ∧ (∃ G : ModuliAutomorphismGroupSpace T a, ∀ (V : Over S) (c : yoneda.obj V ⟶ G.space.obj.obj), AlgebraicSpace.IsEtale c → LocallyOfFiniteType ((yoneda.preimage (c ≫ G.projection)).left))
lean.note: ModuliIsomSpace packages a representing space, its projection and natural bijections with the isomorphisms of the two pulled-back objects. ModuliAutomorphismGroupSpace adds actual group-space maps with pointwise normalization by composition, identity and inversion. The theorem asserts both representations are locally of finite type on every etale scheme chart. The two added statement dependencies are already landed definitions used verbatim.
